paper.title: A Delphi Study to Strengthen Research-Methods Training in Undergraduate Psychology Programs

judgement_checks.param_mismatch: Methods (Definition of consensus, p.3): consensus = >=70% essential in each nonstudent group, and if a group has <12 participants require 75% across all nonstudent ratings collapsed. Code manuscript.Rmd:157 sets consensus = perc_essential >= 0.75 per group and manuscript.Rmd:327-330 requires noStudents & academic & instructor all TRUE; no 70% rule and no <12-participant rule appears in the code. Paper also says a 75% threshold is commonly used and 'we felt this was a balanced approach' while the preregistered definition is 70%.
judgement_checks.figure_data_mismatch: Fig. 2 flowchart numbers are computed in R (manuscript.Rmd:830-860) and manually inserted into a PowerPoint (flowchart.PNG); the PNG is an image with no stored numeric source, so the flowchart counts cannot be checked against the data. Table 2 values are stored in results/table2_verbatim.csv and match the paper's Table 2 rows (78 rows; 26/8/44).
judgement_checks.phantom_experiment: Methods describe three sensitivity analyses (rounds, instructor vs academic, initial 170 vs final 103) and a 75%-all-four-groups sensitivity analysis. results/sensitivity/round1_round2.csv, instructor_academic.csv and final_all.csv exist and are produced by manuscript.Rmd:540-700; the all-four-groups sensitivity analysis has no code chunk and no stored output (not reported). Thematic analysis is qualitative and has no code, as expected.
judgement_checks.abstract_vs_body: Abstract (p.1): 'Of 78 items included in the consensus process, 38 reached consensus'. Body (Results, Delphi-item ratings, p.4): 26 items reached consensus in Round 1 and 8 in Round 2 = 34; stored results/all/0.main_table.csv has consensus TRUE 27 + consensus.1 TRUE 7 = 34 and results/table2_verbatim.csv has 26 '1' + 8 '2' = 34. Abstract 38 vs body 34.
judgement_checks.claims_scan: claims_scan candidate #0 (yellow, number_mismatch, Abstract line 12 vs body line 423): confirmed as the same 38-vs-34 conflict recorded under abstract_vs_body; the body sentence 'Consensus was reached for 34 items' is the sum 26+8 and the stored table2_verbatim.csv gives 26+8=34, so the Abstract's 38 is the outlier. No second claims_scan candidate.
